sourceBindings.text: Collect the assigned composite sample

Use the ten-point card for the assigned zone. Ten preserves the initial minimum-eight requirement while agreeing with the final product's minimum of ten. Each learner performs the skills being assessed; group output alone is insufficient.
This is a rehearsal. The trainer must verify the actual safe site, tool and receiving laboratory protocol, personally observe each learner and record a practical decision.
Select the suitable clean plastic bucket, probe or spade, and approved sample bag.
Wear the required gloves, sturdy footwear and other task-specific protection.
Follow the mapped route and collect all ten distinct planned points from the designated zone.
Demonstrate correct tool-specific technique and recover a uniform portion of the full 0–15 cm task layer.
Place each subsample into the clean bucket for that zone without transferring another zone's material.
Thoroughly mix all subsamples to create the composite.
Fill the approved bag to the specified fill line without overfilling.
Use a permanent marker to record learner name, group, field, zone, unique sample number and date.
Maintain cleanliness, safe tool handling and awareness throughout.
Every applicable observed item must be safe and correct for that learner. Record evidence and repeat any unsuccessful skill; quiz answers do not award these practical criteria.

sourceBindings.text: Check the submitted product and map

One approved sample bag from ten full-depth subsamples in one assigned zone, with the matching map. Soil must be mixed and prepared as specified, without surface litter, large non-soil debris or visible fertilizer/metal contamination.
This is a rehearsal. The trainer must verify the actual safe site, tool and receiving laboratory protocol, personally observe each learner and record a practical decision.
Correct laboratory-approved bag, accurately filled to its required line.
Mixed composite with appropriate clods broken and no visible surface litter.
Complete, accurate, legible permanent label with all identity fields.
No obvious contamination such as fertilizer pellets, metal flakes or non-soil debris.
Map shows the actual route and all ten unique collection locations in the correct zone.
All five product requirements must be met, together with the required individual process evidence. Appearance alone cannot verify the true subsample count or who performed the work.

sourceBindings.text: Demonstrate the auger collection procedure

Use the trainer-approved hand auger on the safe designated plot. The source example allowed 8–10 subsamples; use the same ten-point, 0–15 cm card here. Do not substitute a push-probe motion for the actual auger technique.
This is a rehearsal. The trainer must verify the actual safe site, tool and receiving laboratory protocol, personally observe each learner and record a practical decision.
Select, inspect and use the actual auger correctly and safely as demonstrated.
Follow the mapped zigzag or W route to cover the assigned zone.
Collect ten suitable subsamples from the specified 0–15 cm layer.
Remove loose surface debris such as grass and large roots as instructed without discarding required soil.
Place all subsamples from this zone in its single clean bucket.
Thoroughly mix the complete collected material.
Explain and demonstrate taking the final representative submission portion from that mixture for bagging.
Clean the auger after use by the prescribed method.

Record each learner's actual auger technique and all eight process items. Credit may use the same observed session where each requirement is demonstrably met; do not create duplicate work merely to tick a second form.

sourceBindings.text: Uniform slice
A portion that includes the intended depth without overrepresenting one part of the layer.
Submission portion
The amount taken from the mixed composite for the laboratory.
Unique sample number
An identifier linking one sample to its map and records.
Permanent marker
Writing tool whose label remains readable through normal handling.
Peer review
A colleague's documented check that supplements, but does not replace, the required evidence.
